key_insight: SANA-WM is a 2.6B-parameter open-source world model that natively generates high-fidelity, minute-long 720p videos with precise camera control, matching the visual quality of much larger industrial systems while using far less compute.
problem_solved: Existing video/world models either target short clips or require very large models and heavy compute to produce minute-scale, high-resolution videos with controllable camera motion; SANA-WM addresses efficiency and controllability for minute-scale generation.
method: Hybrid Linear Attention: combines frame-wise Gated DeltaNet (GDN) with softmax attention to capture long-range temporal dependencies with reduced complexity.
Native minute-scale training: architecture and training objectives tuned to produce coherent, high-fidelity 720p videos up to one minute long.

Efficiency-first design: a 2.6B-parameter model plus system-level optimizations to deliver comparable visual quality to larger baselines (e.g., LingBot-World, HY-WorldPlay) at much lower compute cost, with explicit camera-control modules.
impact: Enables researchers and engineers to train and deploy minute-scale, controllable video world models without massive infrastructure, lowering barriers for long-horizon simulation, content creation, and embodied agent research.

paper_title: SANA-WM: Efficient Minute-Scale World Modeling with Hybrid Linear Diffusion Transformer
paper_authors: Haoyi Zhu, Haozhe Liu, Yuyang Zhao, Tian Ye, Junsong Chen
